thread:
evan: Heads-up: planning a staging->prod rollout tonight at 22:30 UTC for release 1.9.0. Need a concise internal announcement (one para + safety bullets) and a rollback owner. Also we want the streaming optimization feature behind a flag (ff.streaming-opt) so we can toggle if needed.

harper: I can write the blurb. Quick Q: are we doing a 10% traffic canary or region-based canary?

evan: Both: 10% traffic in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 15m, then regional ramp if healthy. Include canary traffic fraction in the note.

maya: ops-oncall will take rollback. I'll be secondary for phone escalation. For criteria, propose: sustained >=2% absolute increase in 5xx over baseline for 3m OR p95 increase >250ms for 5m OR >1% drop in eval pass rate on the canary prompt set.

ops-oncall: ok ops-oncall assigned as primary. If we trigger, we'll run `deploybot rollback --to v1.8.4` and/or `ff toggle ff.streaming-opt off` depending on root cause. Please document which to prefer in the blurb.

julian: Note: some enterprise customers have model pins; we should mention we'll not auto-override pinned customers and will contact account teams if we need to coordinate a rollback for them.

aditya: I'll add a short post-deploy compatibility check for dedicated infra (3 checks: baseline throughput, kv-cache hit rate, and model hash match).

harper: Draft blurb below — please edit: "Deploying release 1.9.0 at 22:30 UTC (feature flag ff.streaming-opt enabled by default). This release adds streaming kernel optimizations and a routing tweak to improve throughput on long inputs. Canary: 10% traffic in us-east-1 + eu-west-1 for 15m, then regional ramp. Rollback owner: ops-oncall (primary), maya (secondary). Rollback triggers: sustained >=2% absolute increase in 5xx for 3 minutes, p95 latency increase >250ms for 5 minutes, or >1% regression on the canary eval prompts. Rollback actions: prefer toggling ff.streaming-opt off for config issues; use `deploybot rollback --to v1.8.4` for binary/model-related issues. For enterprise pinned customers we will not auto-change pins; account teams will be contacted. Monitoring: https://grafana.redwood/streams, https://alerts.redwood/slo/1.9.0"

maya: nit: change "enabled by default" -> "enabled for non-pinned traffic". Also call out endpoints: /v1/stream and /v1/chat for clarity.

aditya: add runbook snippet so oncall can copy-paste: ```
# rollback steps
deploybot status --release 1.9.0
ff get ff.streaming-opt
ff toggle ff.streaming-opt off
deploybot rollback --to v1.8.4  # if models/binaries are the issue
```

julian: Add line about release notes: we'll include a public-friendly one-liner in the release notes and attach the sample rerank diffs to internal notes if there are wording-only changes.

evan: Good. Harper, can you include the small runbook snippet and the note about non-pinned traffic? After that I'll post to #all-hands + #eng-releases.

harper: Updated blurb: "Deploying release 1.9.0 at 22:30 UTC. Changes: streaming kernel optimizations + routing fixes to improve long-context throughput. Feature flag ff.streaming-opt enabled for non-pinned traffic; pinned customer traffic is unchanged. Canary: 10% traffic in us-east-1 + eu-west-1 for 15m. Rollback owner: ops-oncall (primary), maya (secondary). Triggers: sustained >=2% absolute 5xx increase for 3m, p95 latency +>250ms for 5m, or >1% drop in canary eval pass rate. Preferred mitigations: toggle ff.streaming-opt off (config), then rollback to v1.8.4 (binary/model) if needed. Quick rollback snippet attached to runbook. Monitoring: https://grafana.redwood/streams, https://alerts.redwood/slo/1.9.0. A public one-line for release notes will be posted separately."

ops-oncall: received. Panels look good. I'll watch the canary for the first 20m and post intent if thresholds cross. Contact: page ops-oncall, then @maya, then call julian if enterprise customers are affected.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted for 1.9.0 by evan. Canary config: us-east-1 (10%), eu-west-1 (10%). Canary timer started. Will report health at +10m.

deploy-bot: CANARY: us-east-1 snapshot: 0.15% 5xx, p95 130ms (baseline 110ms), eval pass 98/100.

aditya: good numbers. watch cache-hit for long contexts.

deploy-bot: CANARY: eu-west-1 snapshot: 0.9% 5xx (baseline 0.2%), p95 380ms (baseline 115ms), eval pass 96/100. Logged rerank diffs: 3 minor phrasing changes.

evan: whoa eu-west spike on p95. ops-oncall, do you want to hold or toggle the flag?

ops-oncall: I'm flagging intent to toggle now. Executing `ff toggle ff.streaming-opt off` — will post confirmation in 30s.

deploy-bot: feature flag update: ff.streaming-opt set to OFF for eu-west-1 by ops-oncall. Observability: https://grafana.redwood/streams?var=region=eu-west-1

deploy-bot: POST-TOGGLE: eu-west-1 5xx 0.12%, p95 125ms, eval pass 97/100. Canary now within thresholds.

harper: Great call. I'll note the flag toggle in the internal blurb and add the sample rerank diffs (not customer-facing).

evan: OK I'm publishing the internal announcement now and pinning the post. Good job team.

deploy-bot: RELEASE: 1.9.0 promoted to prod. Rollback window: 15 minutes from promotion.

julian: I'll notify account teams for pinned customers and run the compatibility sweep with aditya.

aditya: compatibility sweep started: throughput ok, kv-cache hit rate nominal, model hash matches.

evan: Closing thread — ping ops-oncall if you see anomalies and reference this thread timestamp 1749994322.
